newsitem.title: UK: IFC emerging market index approaches 1996 high.
newsitem.headline: IFC emerging market index approaches 1996 high.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation's composite index of emerging market equities, denominated in dollars approached its 1996 ceiling while ING Barings' index broke through last year's high at the start of play on Thursday.
The IFC index climbed 1.3 percent to 305.17 after Wednesday's close, nearing its 1996 high of 308.77 recorded on July 4. It hit a low of 275.79 on January 1 last year.
Day-on-day both Latin America and the Europe, the Middle East and Africa region rose 1.3 percent, to 566.28 and 139.66 respectively, while Asia rose 1.2 percent to 257.58.
The IFC composite index began 1997 at 294.37, after making gains of 7.0 percent over the course of 1996.
ING Barings' Global Emerging Market Index (BEMI), also denominated in dollars BFFO, broke through its 1996 high of 165.948 by the close of Wednesday's trade, rising 1.38 percent day-on-day to 166.00.
It began 1997 at 159.57, after rising 8.9 percent over the course of 1996 from a low of 148.85.
Morgan Stanley's dollar-denominated Emerging Markets Free index was up 1.09 percent at 487.218, calculated after the close of trade on Tuesday.
It began 1997 at 476.315 after making gains of 3.9 percent over 1996. It touched a high last year of 505.452 on July 4, and recorded its 458.369 low on January 1.

All indices are capitalisation-weighted and are calculated daily. The IFC index measures returns on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 26 emerging market countries. It is updated at 2300 GMT.
The BEMI index measures equity returns without dividends from some 21 emerging market countries, with the latest changes reported by 0900 GMT.
The MSCI Free measures equity returns without dividends from 26 emerging market nations. Changes are reported with one day's lag at 1300 GMT.
The J.P. Morgan emerging market bond index, its returns calculated in dollar terms, rose 0.09 percent to 125.62 by the start of trade on Thursday.
It began 1997 at 124.83 after making gains of 14.86 percent over 1996.
By region, Latin America was up 0.34 percent at 103.40, Asia rose 0.16 to 132.34 and East Europe was down 0.34 at 163.38. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
